references.text: A direct parallel to John 9:16 where a division (σχίσμα) arises among the Jews, with some calling Jesus possessed and mad, while others ask how a possessed person can perform such signs.
The Pharisees in Matthew call Jesus possessed (demon-possessed) to explain his miracles, a similar logic to that used by the group in John 9:16 when they ask how a sinner can perform such signs.
Scribes from Jerusalem accuse Jesus of having Beelzebul and casting out demons by the devil's power, a direct contrast to the question in John 9:16 about how a sinner can perform good signs.
The Jews persecute Jesus because he healed on the Sabbath and accuse him of breaking the Sabbath law, just as the discussion in John 9:16 concerns his failure to keep the Sabbath.
